title: Choose the visual world
question: College Helper: pick the world the sign-up and chat screens are rebuilt in. Keep the lead, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Answer Booklet · كراسة الإجابة
options.lineage: Saudi university exam answer booklets: printed cover form, blue-ruled pages, red margin rule, س / ج numbering
options.thesis: Every conversation is a booklet. You write the question on the next ruled line (س١), the agent writes the answer (ج), and the red margin carries the marks: which course it's about, which sources it read, what it did. No chat bubbles, no floating text box.
options.viewport: Chat: a full-width booklet page. A printed header strip (university · major · date · page number), then the red margin on the start side holding س١ / س٢ numerals and red tick-marks for the agent's steps. Answers are set on the ruling, and the composer is simply the next blank line «س٣:» with the caret on it. Sign-up: the booklet's colored cover, its form boxes (university, major, email) as the actual fields.
options.risk: Exams carry stress for some students, so the warmth has to come from the agent's voice and the calm ink, not from the metaphor. A paper texture or fake handwriting on long text would tip it into kitsch, so it stays flat and print-precise.

raised.raise: Ink discipline: only the booklet's own inks exist (paper, ruling blue, margin red, ballpoint blue, print black). No stray grays, no extra accent.
Bilateral invariant: the margin column flips sides with the script and never collapses, even at 360 px.
Chrome deleted: controls are the form's own marks (boxes, ruled lines, tick marks, a «سلّم» submit stamp), never generic pill buttons.
The ruling IS the baseline grid: line-height equals the rule pitch and every line of text sits on a rule.
Fixed personal furniture: every question carries its number, time and course code like a name plate.

options.label: The Study Plan · الخطة الدراسية
options.lineage: the official study-plan sheet every Saudi student gets: courses by level, codes, credit hours, prerequisite lines
options.thesis: The conversation sits on top of your own study plan. Ask about a course and its cell lights up; answers dock beside the plan and cite the course code.
options.viewport: A level-by-level course grid on the start side, the conversation column on the end side, the active course cell highlighted.
options.risk: The closest to what most runs ship for a 'university tool'. It can tip into a dense dashboard, and it waits on real curriculum data to look alive.

options.label: Study Wayfinding
options.lineage: bilingual airport and metro sign systems: yellow bands, black humanist sans, pictograms, edge-locked arrows
options.thesis: Every answer ends at a junction: one sign band per agent step, and the next decision points ahead (practice set → 10 min, read chapter 3 → 25 min).
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band holding the current question, with answers below as corridors and the next decisions as monumental arrows.
options.case: It fuses cleanly, since bilingual signage is native to Saudi airports and the Riyadh Metro, and it makes the agent's steps very legible. It loses on audience identification: it's a travel world, not a study one.
options.risk: Saturated yellow is tiring over a three-hour reading session, and pictograms crowd Arabic text.

options.label: Gridded Type Specimen
options.case: Students don't identify with a type specimen, and grid-built Latin letterforms have no Arabic counterpart.
options.kept: The ruling is the real baseline grid.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.case: Pure strobe and data noise works against calm study and gives no study identity.
options.kept: Total ink discipline: no stray grays.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.lineage: dance notation, a center staff read upward
options.case: Unreadable to students, and the upward time axis fights chat order.
options.kept: The bilateral mirror is the layout law.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.case: It reads as a dated phone UI, and cropped giant lowercase has no Arabic equivalent.
options.kept: Chrome deleted, so the form's own marks are the controls.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished AI chat app: a conversation sidebar, a centered message column, a composer docked at the bottom. Executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every chat product uses: sidebar, thread, composer.
canonCard.risk: Exactly the 'ChatGPT clone' you said you don't want.
